items.headline: Amazon's influencer programme in India doubles to 2 lakh creators, and most of them live outside the metros
items.summary: Close to 75% of Amazon's creators, and about 70% of the shoppers buying through them, are from non-metro cities. Earnings per creator are up 60% on last year, and creators can now tag Amazon products in YouTube and Pinterest content.

items.headline: YouTube Shopping opens to creators with just 500 subscribers in the UAE, Saudi Arabia and Egypt
items.summary: Eligible creators can tag products in videos, Shorts and livestreams and earn commission on sales, with Amazon as the first retail partner. It is another sign that shopping is becoming a core creator income stream outside the US.

items.headline: Instagram steps up its video push as the fight with TikTok and YouTube heats up
items.summary: Bloomberg reports Instagram is ramping up its video strategy. For creators, it points to more reach and tools for video on Instagram as the three platforms compete for their time.

items.headline: Instagram bets on recognition, not cash, to keep Indian creators from drifting to YouTube
items.summary: Its Rings award gives creators a gold ring around their profile for originality, with no prize money. Dolly Singh was the only Indian in the first group of 25, and analysts say recognition will not replace brand-deal income.

items.headline: AI shopping assistants are citing creators, not brands
items.summary: A study of nearly 4,000 product videos found about 60% of the videos AI recommendation tools cited came from creators, against 10% from brands. Detailed reviews mattered more than polish or view counts.

items.headline: Instagram's Edits app drops series linking and lets creators film over an earlier Reel
items.summary: From 28 October, creators can reuse an earlier Reel's audio and footage when filming a new one, replacing the old way of linking Reels into a series.

items.headline: News creators are winning audiences but struggling to get paid
items.summary: Nearly 60% of Americans regularly get news from social media, yet news creators face cautious brand guidelines and platform reach limits. Many are turning to paid subscriptions instead.

items.headline: Colin and Samir start funding their followers' video ideas
items.summary: The creator mentors launched the Big Idea Fund. The first grant, made with Adobe, gives $25,000 to a creator for a five-part YouTube documentary.

items.headline: A fashion creator turned audience requests into a styling business with 500+ clients
items.summary: A case study in going beyond brand deals: the creator built a paid service out of what followers kept asking for.

items.headline: Dhar Mann to brands: stop treating creators like ad space
items.summary: He brought together 50+ creators and brand marketers to push partnerships built on shared ideas rather than follower counts, with creators involved in the creative from the start.
